Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 503s + token latency spikes since 20:00 UTC

Soojin / all — quick findings from infra side (initial):
- No scheduled maintenance on our side during the window.
- Edge telemetry: increased SYN retries and TCP RSTs terminating some connections to Skybridge egress IP space between 20:02-20:36 UTC; concurrent spikes in our DNS resolver latency (~85th pct went from 18ms -> 420ms).
- We see asymmetric AS path for ~18% of flows to Skybridge AS (two upstream peers show different next-hops); one of those next-hops had a transient route withdrawal at 20:01 UTC and then a fast re-advertise.
- Firewall/proxy logs: a mid-tier proxy device produced TLS handshake timeouts for ~2% of connections in the same window. The proxy was operating under >85% CPU for short bursts — traces attached.

Hypothesis: a combination of asymmetric peering + a proxy device under CPU load caused DNS timeouts and some connection retries, leading to elevated token latency and intermittent 503s (upstream connection failures).

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Remove the suspect intermediate route (force path via primary peer) — Rafael to coordinate with peering infra.
2) Bypass mid-tier proxy for Skybridge IP range for at least 30 minutes to see behavior (hotfix).
3) Increase resolver pool and enable local caching TTL override for Skybridge lookups for short duration.

Attachments: traces-20260529.zip (edge logs + tcpdump snippets)

I can implement steps 2 & 3 now if Rafael gives the route hold. Recommend Ben relay the plan to Skybridge and ask them for traceroutes to confirm asymmetry from their side.

Evelyn
Sr. Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s + token latency spikes since 20:00 UTC

Tara — thanks for the quick heads up and for the pcap. We're actively triaging. Short action plan below and expected timing: 

1) Redwood has identified a transient route withdrawal on one of the upstream peers and a proxy device showing brief CPU saturation.
2) We're going to temporarily bypass the mid-tier proxy for traffic to your IP block and pin routes to the primary peer (hotfix) — targeted rollout in the next 15 minutes.
3) We'll enable resolver cache shadowing for your zone for 30 minutes to reduce DNS lookups.

Expected observable changes: immediate reduction in DNS timeouts, token latency should drop back to baseline within 5-15 minutes of the rollout. We'll monitor the Grafana link you provided and share a short exec-friendly summary when the window closes.

Can you run a quick traceroute from one of your affected app hosts and paste it here? That will help validate the asymmetry. Also, please confirm whether this impacted any single region more than others.

If the mitigation does not reduce errors within 15 minutes, we'll escalate to execs and propose a temporary service credit pending SLA review.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Team — Redwood Inference
